title: Robust tool loop safety and result encoding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: deliver a hardened execution loop for multi-tool chains that supports streaming result injection, preserves structured outputs across compatibility layers, and detects/mitigates recursion or runaway loops. This ticket scopes the runtime + API contract changes, integration tests, and a gradual rollout plan. It emphasizes predictable semantics for idempotent tool calls, deterministic injection ordering for structured outputs, and conservative safety defaults (max depth, token budgets) to protect customer applications.
acceptance_criteria: Execution loop enforces configurable max_call_depth (default=3) and total_tool_invocations_per_request (default=10) with clear error codes (TOOL_LOOP_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, TOOL_INVOKE_LIMIT)
Streaming path supports partial tool results injected as structured chunks; consumer SDKs can rehydrate into the original structured format without custom parsing hacks
A compatibility shim translates legacy flat-string tool outputs into the structured output schema (json-schema v1) for downstream components
Integration tests cover nested tool chains, tool failures mid-stream, and backpressure scenarios with mocked latency profiles
Performance regression <5% p50 latency for standard generation workloads when safety guards are enabled
tasks: Design API spec changes: streaming chunk envelope + result metadata (tool_id, call_id, call_depth, partial_flag)
Implement runtime guardrail: call stack tracker, unique call IDs, and dedup table for idempotency tokens
Add compatibility_layer that maps legacy tool output formats into structured schema with heuristics and confidence metadata
E2E tests: orchestration harness that simulates 5 common tool chain patterns (sequential, fan-out, fan-in, recursive, error-retry)
Update SDKs (python/js) to expose call lifecycle hooks and a safe default client-side max_depth setting
Create observability: per-request call_graph, guardrail_events metric, and dashboard panels
implementation_notes: Use a lightweight callstack hash (sha1 of tool_id sequence + request_id truncated) to detect repeated cycles across streaming chunks
Emit streaming envelopes as newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with small schema: {event_type, tool_id, call_id, depth, payload_type, payload}
Backpressure: if tool is slow, runtime can yield a 'streaming_hold' event to clients and continue; SDKs should surface a retryable wait state
Idempotency: recommend token supplied by caller; runtime will deduplicate identical (token, tool_id) pairs within the request TTL
Compatibility shim will try JSON parse -> key-mapping rules -> fallback to text field and set 'compatibility_confidence' <= 0.5
Defaults chosen conservatively; operator can relax via tenant config (Dedicated/Private) if needed
decisions: Prefer explicit depth guard and clear error codes over silent truncation to avoid surprising downstream logic
Streaming will carry structured metadata to allow partial evaluation tools (e.g., indexers) to consume early results
Compatibility rules will be implemented in a separate translation layer to keep runtime fast and allow iterative updates without full runtime deploy
We will not attempt semantic equivalence between tool results — instead we attach confidence and original_raw to aid downstream reconciliations

qa_plan: Unit tests for callstack tracking and dedup table expiry
Chaos tests: inject intermittent tool timeouts and assert streaming resumes with correct metadata
Compatibility fuzzing: feed 10k legacy outputs into shim and measure parse success and confidence distributions
Performance benchmarks on small and large models with and without guards enabled
rollout_plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag 'tool_loop_safety_v1'; enable for 5% of hosted traffic
Collect metrics for guard triggers, error code rates, and latency impact for 2 weeks
Expand to Dedicated tenants with opt-in until SDK changes land in next minor release
Full enablement once no high-severity regressions and security sign-off
edge_cases: Tool that streams interleaved structured pieces for different logical outputs — runtime must maintain per-call buffers until 'final' chunk
Recursive tool chains where a tool reinvokes the same tool with identical idempotency token — detect as cycle and fail early
Legacy tools that return malformed JSON repeatedly — mark as low confidence and surface original payload to caller
Long-running tool that never emits final chunk: enforce request-level timeout and emit TOOL_STREAM_TIMEOUT
